Arcane has fallen a long way. RIP.

I'll straight up say pass on this one. Gameplay is admittedly decent, a looter shooter the likes of Borderlands with a Vampire coat of paint. Gun play feels solid, and the idea of open world vampire hunting and shooting up cultists is fine enough, but thats mostly where any positives stop. Enemies even on their harder difficulties are laughable. Sure, it was even easier back when it first came out, but even post patch its a breeze. Enemy path finding makes me feel like this was pure after thought, with even now certain enemies just unable to figure out player position and elevation correctly. Dispatching vampires can be awkward, as you need a stake to finish the job or UV light (barring specific hero abilities or some super unique weapon). This alone shouldn't be an issue except for the fact that only certain types of weapons have a stake attachment and specific tech weapons using UV light. Without any hand held stake to melee finish a vampire, you're rather limited or forced to use certain classes of weapons for vampire killing (once again, barring certain hero abilities that can bypass that which will vary from person to person). Story was... mostly forgettable. Very few points while playing did the game have my attention in terms of dialogue, and the cut scenes are just freeze frames of 3d models despite the game itself having animation during game play. Its such a bizarre choice that only further paints this game as a half baked product. For online Co-op, the game balance gets even more thrown out the window as if enemies just weren't properly scaled to take on 2 or more players. When the party is intentionally trying to draw the attention of The Rook (an allegedly punishing opponent for drawing too much attention from the head vampire) to just trash him like hes a side quest boss, something is really off. This game isn't even an indie game, this is suppose to be a AAA experience. This came out the door with a 70 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dollar price tag; and that's the "basic" version not including season pass crap that would demand you a total of about 100 dollars for the full experience. Its beyond shameful, because the ones who pushed this out the door clearly had no shame to hold them back. Now with the developer team effectively terminated, don't expect much more fixing beyond this point. Is it worth playing? At a discount at best, fun was had by myself because I wasn't soloing and got this game on a significant discount. With no further updates in the works, and season pass content cancelled, I don't expect a very active player base to remain playing this if there even is anyone still online. This game is by no means worth the full price.

[h1][i]Bordlerlands[/i] with vampires[/h1]

TLDR, this is basically [i]Borderlands[/i] but with vampires rather than sci fi. I play with not-Gaige who summons a friendly vampire rather than a robot like OG Gaige. 

[h1]If it were sold for $20, it would be a decent buy.[/h1]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3252498949

[b]UPDATE:[/b] Microsoft is apparently planning to release the final patch after all. 

https://x.com/playRedfall/status/1791491460858020040

If this were a $20 indie game, it would be considered a decent AA game with an interesting premise. However, rather than sell it for what it was worth, Microsoft decided to push it out before it was ready (Bethesda style) and then sell it for $70 + Season Pass.

Right now it's in a bundle on Fanatical which means you can get it and another game for $25 which is worth it in my opinion

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

It's an FPS with stealth and way too many guns. If you can imagine Borderlands with more stealth and tougher enemies (the Vampires at least are tougher than the enemies in Borderlands) it's basically that.

One significant minus is that the ammo is expensive and seems hard to find. More ammo, cheaper ammo, or simply ammo that automatically refills between missions would have made this game better. 

[h1]Setting[/h1]

If you liked [i]Evil West[/i] you will probably like the setting of this game. 

This has a gothic, vampire themed setting which I quite like. In particular, I like that you are fighting the vampires rather than being one. It's enjoyably cheesy in a way which more or less matches the tone of [i]The Secret World[/i] but with an emphasis on vampires rather than conspiracy theories. 

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3246518759

If you are fan of [i]Welcome to Nightvale[/i] or Neil Gaiman books like [i]Coraline,[/i] you will probably like it OK. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6kPXH9HJvE

One thing I disliked is that the setting goes too far in my opinion insofar as things have gotten so out of hand that everyone you meet besides your crew is either a Vampire, a cultist working for the vampires, or a literal prisoner waiting to be rescued. It would have been better to use the enemies more sparingly in my opinion to have an atmosphere that would be more mysterious and unsettling as opposed to post-apocalyptic.

[h1]Story[/h1]

Very basic and told via voice-overs, lore items and images rather like the extended cut of the [i]Mass Effect 3[/i] ending. 

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

I really hope that they follow through with their recent announcement to make this playable offline. It's nice to have a gothic, vampire-infested town to sneak around in.
